extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI). User-controlled input from the 'name' query parameter (request) is concatenated into 'content' at line 38, then 'content' is passed directly to jinja2.Template(content).render() at line 41. Because the user input becomes part of the template source itself, an attacker can inject Jinja2 expressions such as ?name={{7*6}} or ?name={{config}} / {{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()}} to read sensitive data or achieve remote code execution. The commented-out test at tests/test_main.py:38-41 (?name={{7*6}}) confirms this attack surface.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS). The 'name' query parameter is interpolated unescaped into an HTML f-string and returned via HTMLResponse without any sanitization or escaping. Jinja2's Template().render() here does NOT autoescape because content is the template source, not the rendered context, so an attacker can supply ?name=<script>alert(1)</script> to inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript executed in the victim's browser. The 'public_ip' value fetched from an external service is also reflected unescaped.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

extra.message: Hardcoded secret token. SUPER_SECRET_TOKEN is assigned a hardcoded literal value ('5u93R53Cr3tT0k3n') in source code instead of being loaded from the environment. Hardcoded credentials committed to source control can be extracted by anyone with repository access and cannot be rotated without a code change.

Hardcoded sensitive value. SUPER_SECRET_NAME is assigned a hardcoded literal ('John Ripper') in source code rather than loaded from the environment (as the FIXME comment indicates). Sensitive configuration values should not be embedded in source code.

Security misconfiguration: FastAPI application is instantiated with debug=config.DEBUG, where DEBUG is controlled by an environment variable. When enabled in a production environment, debug mode can expose detailed stack traces, internal application state, and sensitive configuration information to remote users, aiding attackers in reconnaissance.

Outbound request to a URL sourced from environment configuration (PUBLIC_IP_SERVICE_URL) whose response body is then reflected directly back into the HTTP response to the user (public_ip at line 36/38). While the URL itself is from config rather than direct user input, the response is returned verbatim and unescaped, and the request has no timeout configured (potential for resource exhaustion / hanging requests). This pattern of reflecting an external service's untrusted response into the page is dangerous.
